chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not employ foolish wet-nurses, for the milk affects [the child], and the boy is drawn to the milk, meaning to the wet-nurse with regards to frivolity and foolishness.'

key_terms.اللَّبَنَ: Milk (specifically breast milk in this context)

ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid employing foolish wet-nurses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of 'nutritional transmission' (ta'thir), positing that a wet-nurse's intellectual and moral qualities, specifically 'rumuna' (frivolity or lack of depth), are transferred to the child through her milk. It underscores the significance of selecting a wet-nurse not merely for physical nourishment but for her character, as the child's attachment to her leads to the inheritance of her cognitive traits.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not employ foolish wet-nurses, for the milk affects, and the boy is drawn to the milk, meaning to the wet-nurse with regards to the frivolity and the foolishness’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim and Jamil ibn Darraj and Sa‘d ibn abu Khalaf who has said the following:
“About the case of a woman who has a servant who has committed fornication and we need her milk. He (the Imam) said, ‘Instruct her to give permission, the milk will be fine.’”
